entries.note: “Stand on their own” supplies no shared criterion for the capabilities or applications at issue.

entries.test: Public technical descriptions of leading AI systems through July 2025 would establish whether they increasingly incorporated symbolic components and publicly acknowledged that shift as neurosymbolic AI.
entries.note: The surrounding examples give the claimed shift a concrete architectural meaning.

entries.test: Public research on AI research allocation and comparative reliability of purely neural and alternative systems would test whether concentrating effort on the former contributed to current LLM unreliability.
entries.note: The normalization narrows the claimed consequences by omitting internet degradation and replacement of humans with unreliable systems.

entries.test: OpenAI’s 2023 Code Interpreter documentation and recordings or transcripts of Hinton’s remarks would establish the implementation, timing, and correspondence with his criticism.
entries.note: Marcus himself asserts the comparison with Hinton’s position.

entries.test: Public timed demonstrations comparing o3 using symbolic code with Marcus constructing comparable valid crossword grids without writing code would test the speed claim.
entries.note: “Can” describes an existing capability here, rather than an uncertain future possibility.

entries.test: The Grok 4 Humanity’s Last Exam results and underlying training-resource measurements would show whether tool-free performance gains diminished while scores remained far below the benchmark maximum.
entries.note: The graph supplies a concrete context for the otherwise expansive language about superintelligence.

entries.test: Public implementation descriptions of test-time scaling would establish whether it uses symbolic iteration and aggregation techniques.
entries.note: The qualification limits his asserted knowledge; it does not explicitly assign a probability.
His lack of conviction is a private belief. He does not assert that the field definitely lacks the right architecture.

entries.test: Public task evaluations and comparable o3-versus-o1 hallucination measurements available for the July 2025 systems would establish the claimed performance differences.
entries.note: The comparison is explicitly limited to some tasks and the systems at publication.
The necessity claim is explicitly qualified by “likely”; the research-attention claim does not remove that hedge.
The context supports interpreting the destination as AGI, but the remaining distance is expressly qualified by “likely.”
“It would appear” makes the causal account tentative. “In desperation” also attributes a motive.

entries.test: Public evaluations comparing generated-code correctness on familiar training-like tasks and materially novel tasks would test the claimed dependence on training-example similarity and occurrence of failures.
entries.note: Here “can be buggy” describes observable failure behavior, rather than forecasting an uncertain event.
The preceding sentence says further breakthroughs will “likely” be needed; the normalization makes their necessity categorical. The recommendation remains a judgment about the best approach.
“Pierce the scaling narrative” does not specify whether the outcome is logical contradiction, changed investor beliefs, or diminished public acceptance.

entries.test: Public OpenAI tool-use evaluations and statements through publication would establish whether combining neural models with symbolic tools improved performance without OpenAI acknowledging this as support for neurosymbolic AI.
entries.note: In context, “vindicated” refers to demonstrated benefits of combining neural and symbolic components. “Accidentally” describes the ironic outcome rather than a separately evidenced private intention.
This is a qualified recommendation to support neurosymbolic AI and pay attention to its development.
